acceptanceCriteria: Stage counts are monotone non-increasing and sum with drops to the candidate count.
Existing coverage fields and their pinned values in cmd/corvint tests are unchanged.
An old consumer ignoring the new field still parses the packet.
body: Owner requested this on 2026-09-23 after reviewing Tencent/WeKnora (MIT) as prior art; this ticket records an idea, not delivery or promotion. Original Go work only; no source import. WeKnora is an LLM-at-ingest, database-backed RAG platform, so only the mechanism is borrowed and it must stay deterministic, local and read-only under AGENTS.md invariants 4 and 7. Before implementation is called complete, update the owning indexed spec with stable requirements, non-goals, failure modes, acceptance evidence and rollback, and finish normal CEM/OCM, independent review and mandatory gates. Prior art: website-docs/02-architecture/04-rag-pipeline.md and 03-features/16-observability.md of https://github.com/Tencent/WeKnora. Each pipeline stage (query understanding, parallel search, rerank, merge, top-k filter) emits progress with result counts, and document parsing is shown as a span tree with per-stage timing. Current state: the packet coverage block reports aggregate `candidates`, `excluded_sources`, `omitted_results`, `unparsed_sources` and `within_budget`, so a consumer cannot tell whether a missing row died at the relevance floor, at fusion, at merge or at the byte budget. Idea: add an ordered per-stage count (candidates, after floor, after fusion, after merge, after budget) with the dominant drop reason per stage, additive to the existing coverage fields. This extends invariant 1 from explaining inclusion to explaining exclusion and is the drill-down V1-0023 needs. Owning spec: docs/specs/task-context-packet-v0.md. Related: V1-0023.
title: context: per-stage candidate drop accounting in the coverage block
